examples.en: A costume parade was held in the street during the festival.

examples.ko: 아이들이 동화 속 인물로 분장하고 가장행렬에 참가했어요.
examples.en: The children dressed up as fairy-tale characters and joined the costume parade.
People gathered along the road to watch the costume parade.
This year's costume parade was more colorful than ever.

examples.ko: 우리 반은 가장행렬에서 로봇 옷을 입기로 했어요.
examples.en: Our class decided to wear robot costumes in the parade.
After the costume parade ends, the fireworks begin.

explain: 사람들이 분장이나 변장을 하고 줄지어 걷는 행사예요. 그냥 줄지어 걷는 행사는 '행진'이나 '퍼레이드'라고 하고, 분장이 중요할 때 '가장행렬'이라고 해요. 축제나 학교 행사 이야기에 나와요.
explain_en: It is an event where people walk in a line wearing costumes or disguises. A plain march is called '행진' or '퍼레이드', and '가장행렬' is used when the costumes are the point. It comes up in talk about festivals and school events.

examples.ko: 관객들은 공연이 끝나자 큰 갈채를 보냈어요.
examples.en: The audience gave a big round of applause when the show ended.

examples.ko: 선수들은 팬들의 갈채 속에 경기장에 들어섰어요.
examples.en: The players entered the stadium amid the fans' cheers.
The clapping and cheering went on for a long time.
It was a wonderful performance that deserved acclaim.

examples.ko: 그는 갈채는 바라지 않고 묵묵히 일했어요.
examples.en: He worked quietly without wanting any praise.
His effort was rewarded with enthusiastic applause.

explain: '박수'는 손뼉 치는 행동이고, '갈채'는 소리 내어 크게 칭찬하는 뜻까지 담겨요. '갈채를 보내다/받다'로 쓰고, 말할 때는 보통 '박수'를 쓰며 '박수갈채'라는 짝말로도 자주 나와요.
explain_en: '박수' is the act of clapping, while '갈채' also carries the sense of loud praise. It is used as '갈채를 보내다/받다', and in speech people usually just say '박수'. It also appears in the pair '박수갈채'.

en: open; begin (a festival, season, or event)

examples.en: The Olympics open next week.
The festival opened on Friday evening.

examples.ko: 프로야구가 개막하면 매주 경기장에 갈 거예요.
examples.en: Once the pro baseball season starts, I'll go to the stadium every week.

examples.ko: 영화제가 개막하는 날 많은 배우가 왔어요.
examples.en: Many actors came on the day the film festival opened.

examples.ko: 공연이 개막해서 극장 앞이 사람들로 붐볐어요.
examples.en: The show opened, and the front of the theater was crowded with people.

examples.ko: 전시회가 개막할 때까지 준비할 게 많아요.
examples.en: There is a lot to prepare before the exhibition opens.

explain: 축제, 경기, 공연, 전시처럼 큰 행사가 시작될 때 써요. 반대말은 '폐막하다'예요. 수업이나 회의에는 '시작하다'를 쓰고 '개막하다'는 쓰지 않아요. '개막식', '개막 경기'처럼 명사로도 많이 써요.
explain_en: Used when a big event such as a festival, sports season, show, or exhibition begins. The opposite is 폐막하다. For classes or meetings use 시작하다, not 개막하다. Nouns like 개막식 and 개막 경기 are common.

p.n: Same meaning; the passive version sounds more impersonal.

examples.ko: 공중제비를 멋지게 돈 선수가 금메달을 땄어요.
examples.en: The athlete who did a great somersault won the gold medal.

examples.ko: 공중제비는 처음 배울 때 조금 무서워요.
examples.en: Somersaults in the air are a little scary when you first learn them.

examples.ko: 공중제비 한 번에 관중이 박수를 쳤어요.
examples.en: The audience clapped after one single somersault.
I tried doing a somersault at the swimming pool.
My older brother can even do a somersault.
I fell while doing a somersault and hurt my wrist.

explain: 몸을 공중에서 거꾸로 한 바퀴 돌리는 동작이에요. 보통 '공중제비를 돌다'처럼 '돌다'와 함께 써요. 바닥에서 구르는 '앞구르기'와는 달리 몸이 공중에 떠서 도는 동작이에요.
explain_en: This is the move of flipping your body upside down once in the air. It is usually used with '돌다', as in '공중제비를 돌다'. Unlike '앞구르기' (a forward roll on the ground), the body is in the air while turning.

examples.en: The soldiers run around the field every dawn.

examples.ko: 방독면을 쓰고 구보하라는 명령이 가장 힘들었어요.
examples.en: The order to run while wearing a gas mask was the hardest.

examples.ko: 신병들이 아침마다 삼십 분씩 구보하면 체력이 좋아져요.
examples.en: If recruits run for thirty minutes every morning, their stamina improves.

examples.ko: 무거운 배낭을 메고 구보해서 어깨가 아파요.
examples.en: I ran carrying a heavy backpack, so my shoulders hurt.

examples.ko: 학생들이 선생님을 따라 줄을 맞춰 구보했어요.
examples.en: The students ran in line, following the teacher.

examples.ko: 어제는 비가 와서 실내에서 구보하지 못했어요.
examples.en: It rained yesterday, so we couldn't run indoors.

explain: '달리다'보다 훈련하듯 일정한 속도로 달리는 느낌이 있고, 군대나 훈련 이야기에서 주로 써요. 구령으로는 '구보!'처럼 짧게 말하기도 해요. 취미로 달릴 때는 '뛰다', '달리다'가 자연스러워요.
explain_en: Compared with '달리다', it feels like running at a steady pace as training, and it mostly appears in military or drill contexts. As a command it can be shouted short, as '구보!'. For running as a hobby, '뛰다' or '달리다' sounds more natural.

examples.en: The military band started playing as it marched down the street.

examples.ko: 국군의 날 행사에서 군악대 공연을 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw a military band performance at the Armed Forces Day event.
My uncle served in the military band in the army.

examples.ko: 군악대의 북소리에 맞춰 사람들이 박수를 쳤어요.
examples.en: People clapped along to the drumbeat of the military band.

examples.ko: 이번 주말에 공원에서 군악대 연주회가 열린대요.
examples.en: I heard a military band concert is being held in the park this weekend.
I have a friend who played the trumpet in a military band.

explain: 일반 악단은 '밴드'나 '악단'이라고 하지만, 군악대는 군대 소속으로 행사나 의식에서 연주하는 팀을 말할 때 써요. 행사 때 함께 나오는 '의장대'는 연주보다 절도 있는 동작과 의식을 맡아요.
explain_en: A regular group is called a '밴드' or '악단', but 군악대 is used for the team that belongs to the military and plays at ceremonies and events. The '의장대' (honor guard) often appears at the same events, but it focuses on precise drill and ritual rather than playing music.

examples.ko: 밤이 되자 거리의 네온사인이 하나둘 켜졌어요.
examples.en: When night fell, the neon signs on the street lit up one by one.
The neon sign in front of the shop keeps flickering.
I walked slowly under the glow of the neon signs.
Every building has flashy neon signs up.
There are many shops decorated with neon signs.
The glow of the neon signs was reflected on the wet street.

explain: 밤거리나 가게 간판을 말할 때 자주 나오는 외래어예요. 밤의 번화가 분위기를 말할 때 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It is a loanword that often comes up when describing night streets and shop signs. It fits well when describing the atmosphere of a busy downtown at night.

examples.ko: 마을 잔치에 농악대가 와서 신나게 연주했어요.
examples.en: A nongak band came to the village feast and played with great spirit.
Hearing the nongak band's drums made my shoulders move.
The children walked along following the nongak band.

examples.ko: 저는 대학교 때 농악대에서 꽹과리를 쳤어요.
examples.en: In college I played the kkwaenggwari in a nongak band.
On the first day of the festival there is a nongak band performance.
I took a photo together with the nongak band.

explain: 농악은 꽹과리, 징, 장구, 북으로 흥겹게 연주하며 노는 우리 전통 음악이고, 농악대는 그것을 연주하는 사람들의 무리예요. '풍물패'라고도 하며 축제나 마을 행사에서 자주 볼 수 있어요.
explain_en: Nongak is traditional Korean music played with the kkwaenggwari, jing, janggu and drum, and 농악대 is the group that plays it. It is also called '풍물패', and you often see one at festivals and village events.

en: one-man show; sole domination of the stage

examples.en: Today's game was that player's show.
The awards ceremony turned into that film's night.

examples.ko: 이 분야는 오랫동안 한국 선수들의 독무대예요.
examples.en: This field has long been dominated by Korean athletes.
It was my uncle's show until the party ended.
At karaoke, my sister takes over the stage.
In this competition, a newcomer made the stage entirely her own.

explain: 한 사람이나 한 팀이 다른 사람은 끼어들지 못할 만큼 눈에 띄고 압도할 때 써요. 보통 '~의 독무대'라고 말하고, 경기·시상식·모임에서 자주 나와요. 칭찬일 수도 있고 그냥 상황 설명일 수도 있어요.
explain_en: Use it when one person or team stands out so much that nobody else gets a chance. It's usually said as '~의 독무대' and often appears for games, award shows and gatherings. It can be praise or just a description of the situation.

examples.en: I watched amazing stunts at the circus.

examples.ko: 강아지가 공을 받는 묘기를 보여 줬어요.
examples.en: The puppy showed a trick of catching a ball.
That player performs tricks with a soccer ball.
The children clapped for the stunt.
I practice every day to enter the stunt contest.
The bicycle stunts were really thrilling.

explain: 사람이나 동물이 연습해서 보여 주는 놀라운 재주예요. '재능'은 타고난 능력이고, '묘기'는 눈앞에서 보여 주는 기술이에요. '묘기를 부리다'나 '묘기를 보여 주다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is an amazing skill that a person or animal has practiced and shows off. 재능 is natural talent, while 묘기 is a skill performed in front of people. It goes with verbs like 묘기를 부리다 and 묘기를 보여 주다.

examples.ko: 올림픽 성화 봉송이 우리 동네를 지나갔어요.
examples.en: The Olympic torch relay passed through our neighborhood.

examples.ko: 성화 봉송 주자로 뽑혀서 정말 기뻐요.
examples.en: I'm so happy I was chosen as a torch relay runner.

examples.ko: 봉송 행사 때문에 시내 도로가 막혔어요.
examples.en: The roads downtown were blocked because of the relay event.
Yesterday I went out from morning to watch the torch relay.

examples.ko: 성화 봉송은 몇 달 동안 이어졌어요.
examples.en: The torch relay continued for several months.

examples.ko: 이번 봉송에는 시민 천 명이 참여해요.
examples.en: A thousand citizens are taking part in this relay.

explain: 일상에서는 거의 '성화 봉송'처럼 올림픽 이야기에서 만나요. 선물이나 물건을 보내는 일에는 쓰지 않고 '보내다', '배송'을 써요.
explain_en: In daily life you mostly meet it in '성화 봉송' (torch relay) in talk about the Olympics. For sending gifts or goods, people use '보내다' or '배송' instead.

examples.ko: 우리 학교에서 피아노 삼중주 연주회가 열려요.
examples.en: A piano trio concert is being held at our school.

examples.ko: 바이올린, 첼로, 피아노로 이루어진 삼중주를 들었어요.
examples.en: I listened to a trio made up of violin, cello and piano.

examples.ko: 삼중주는 세 사람이 연주해서 소리가 풍성해요.
examples.en: A trio is played by three people, so the sound is rich.

examples.ko: 동생은 친구 둘과 삼중주 팀을 만들었어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling formed a trio with two friends.

examples.ko: 오늘 공연에서 삼중주 곡이 가장 좋았어요.
examples.en: The trio piece was my favorite in today's concert.
Arranged as a trio, the song sounds fresh.

explain: 세 명이 각자 다른 악기나 성부를 맡아 함께 연주하는 것을 말해요. 두 명이면 '이중주', 네 명이면 '사중주'예요. 팀 이름으로는 '트리오'도 많이 써요.
explain_en: This is when three players each take a different instrument or part. With two it is '이중주', and with four it is '사중주'. For a group's name, '트리오' is also used often.

examples.en: My father plays the saxophone as a hobby.
I like the saxophone because its sound is smooth.
I play jazz on the saxophone.
Is the saxophone hard to blow?
The saxophone sounds lower than the trumpet.
I want to learn the saxophone and the piano together.

explain: 악기마다 쓰는 동사가 달라서 색소폰은 '불다', 피아노는 '치다', 바이올린은 '켜다'를 써요. '연주하다'는 어느 악기에도 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: Each instrument has its own verb: 불다 for the saxophone, 치다 for the piano, and 켜다 for the violin. 연주하다 works for any instrument.

examples.ko: 기자는 불이 난 현장에서 생중계를 하고 있어요.
examples.en: The reporter is broadcasting live from the scene of the fire.

examples.ko: 월드컵 경기를 생중계로 보려고 일찍 일어났어요.
examples.en: I got up early to watch the World Cup match live.

examples.ko: 오늘 밤 시상식은 생중계를 하지 않는대요.
examples.en: I heard they won't broadcast tonight's award ceremony live.
The sound suddenly cut out during the live broadcast.
I started a live stream on my phone for the fans.

examples.ko: 생중계는 실수해도 다시 할 수 없어서 긴장돼요.
examples.en: With live coverage you can't redo mistakes, so I get nervous.

explain: '생방송'은 방송 프로그램이 지금 나가는 것을 말하고, '생중계'는 경기나 행사나 사건의 현장을 그 자리에서 바로 보여 주는 것을 말해요. 보통 '생중계를 하다', '생중계로 보다'로 써요.
explain_en: '생방송' means a program going out live, while '생중계' means showing a game, event or incident right as it happens on the spot. It is usually used as '생중계를 하다' or '생중계로 보다'.

examples.en: The church at dawn is quiet and sacred.

examples.ko: 그 사람들에게 이 산은 성스러운 곳이에요.
examples.en: This mountain is a sacred place to those people.
I listened for a long time to the solemnly ringing bell.

examples.ko: 아이를 안은 어머니의 모습이 성스러워 보였어요.
examples.en: The mother holding her child looked sacred.

examples.ko: 성스럽다고 하는 곳일수록 예의를 지켜야 해요.
examples.en: The more a place is called sacred, the more you must show respect.
I couldn't capture that sacred moment in a photo.

explain: 종교적인 장소나 순간처럼 깨끗하고 높게 느껴지는 대상에 써요. '성스러운 곳', '성스러운 의식'처럼 뒤에 오는 명사를 꾸미는 모양이 많아요. ㅂ 불규칙이라 '성스러워요', '성스러운'으로 바뀌어요.
explain_en: It is used for things that feel pure and elevated, such as religious places or moments. The modifier form appears a lot, as in '성스러운 곳' and '성스러운 의식'. It is ㅂ-irregular, changing to '성스러워요' and '성스러운'.

examples.en: Many people go on a pilgrimage to holy sites every year.
He walked an old road in Spain on a pilgrimage.

examples.ko: 순례하는 사람들이 작은 마을에서 쉬어 갔어요.
examples.en: Pilgrims rested in the small village.
Someday I want to visit famous temples on a pilgrimage.
I took many photos while touring the historic sites.

examples.ko: 먼 길을 순례할 때는 편한 신발이 필요해요.
examples.en: You need comfortable shoes when going on a long pilgrimage.

explain: 종교적인 성지를 찾아다니며 기도하는 여행이에요. 요즘에는 좋아하는 드라마 촬영지나 맛집을 돌아다니는 일도 '성지순례', '맛집 순례'처럼 가볍게 말해요. 보통 한 곳이 아니라 여러 곳을 차례로 돌아본다는 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.en: fan pilgrimage to a filming location
phrases.nuance_ko: 원래는 종교 성지를 찾는 말인데, 요즘은 팬들이 좋아하는 작품의 장소를 찾아가는 일에도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Originally about visiting religious holy sites, it is now also used for fans visiting places connected to a favorite work.

explain_en: It is a trip to religious holy sites to pray. These days people also lightheartedly use '성지순례' or '맛집 순례' for visiting favorite drama locations or restaurants. It usually feels like visiting several places in turn, not just one.

en: live broadcast/recording; scene as it happens

examples.ko: 오늘 저녁에 콘서트 실황이 텔레비전에서 나와요.
examples.en: The live concert is on television this evening.
I listened to the live baseball game on the radio.

examples.ko: 이 앨범에는 지난해 서울 공연 실황이 담겨 있어요.
examples.en: This album contains a live recording of last year's Seoul concert.

examples.ko: 실황 중계를 보려고 일찍 자리에 앉았어요.
examples.en: I sat down early to watch the live broadcast.
Because it is a live broadcast, even mistakes go out as they are.

examples.ko: 녹화가 아니라 실황이라서 실수해도 다시 못 해요.
examples.en: It is live, not recorded, so I cannot redo it even if I make a mistake.

explain: 그 자리에서 벌어지는 모습을 그대로 전한다는 느낌이라 '실황 중계', '공연 실황'처럼 방송이나 앨범 이름에 많이 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '생중계'나 '라이브'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It carries the feel of showing what happens on the spot as it is, so it appears a lot in broadcast and album titles like '실황 중계' and '공연 실황'. In everyday talk people also say '생중계' or '라이브'.

en: toss about; have a close game

examples.en: The two players traded the lead and finally tied.
The class rankings flip-flop with every exam.
I was worried and tossed and turned all night.
It was such a back-and-forth game that I watched to the end.
The two candidates keep overtaking each other.

examples.ko: 강아지 두 마리가 바닥에서 엎치락뒤치락하며 놀아요.
examples.en: Two puppies play, rolling over each other on the floor.

explain: 경기나 선거처럼 서로 앞서고 뒤바뀌는 접전에 쓰고, 순위가 계속 오르내릴 때도 써요. 잠을 못 자고 뒤척일 때는 '뒤척이다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is used for close contests like games and elections where the lead keeps changing, and also when rankings keep going up and down. For tossing and turning in bed, people also say '뒤척이다'.

examples.ko: 모임이 끝난 뒤 여흥으로 노래를 불렀어요.
examples.en: After the gathering, we sang songs for fun.

examples.ko: 회식 때 여흥 시간에 장기 자랑을 했어요.
examples.en: At the company dinner, we did a talent show during the fun time.
A feast is a bit dull without some entertainment.
The host told jokes to liven up the fun.

examples.ko: 졸업식이 끝나고 여흥은 학생들이 직접 준비했어요.
examples.en: After the graduation ceremony, the students prepared the entertainment themselves.

examples.ko: 여흥에 빠져서 시간 가는 줄 몰랐어요.
examples.en: I was so caught up in the fun that I lost track of time.

explain: 잔치나 모임에서 본 행사가 끝난 뒤, 또는 중간에 즐기려고 하는 노래, 춤, 놀이를 말할 때 써요. 그냥 '재미'가 아니라 행사의 곁들이라는 느낌이 있어요. 일상에서는 '뒤풀이'나 '놀이'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It refers to songs, dances, and games enjoyed during or after the main part of a party or gathering. It is not plain 'fun' but a sideline to an event. In daily life people also say '뒤풀이' or '놀이'.

examples.ko: 율동적인 음악에 맞춰 아이들이 춤을 췄어요.
examples.en: The children danced to the rhythmic music.
The waves rolled in and out rhythmically.

examples.ko: 이 그림은 선이 율동적이라서 살아 움직이는 것 같아요.
examples.en: The lines in this painting are so rhythmic that it seems alive.
He is a person whose rhythmic stride stands out.

examples.ko: 시의 율동적인 느낌을 소리 내어 읽으며 느껴 봤어요.
examples.en: I felt the rhythmic quality of the poem by reading it aloud.

examples.ko: 율동적인 동작을 따라 하니까 운동이 돼요.
examples.en: Following the rhythmic movements works as exercise.

explain: '율동'은 유치원에서 노래에 맞춰 하는 춤 동작을 가리킬 때도 많이 써요. '율동적'은 말투가 조금 딱딱해서 일상에서는 '리듬감 있는'이라고 하는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: '율동' is also widely used for the simple dance moves kids do to songs at kindergarten. '율동적' sounds a bit stiff, so in everyday speech people often say '리듬감 있는' instead.

examples.ko: 주말에 미술 전람회를 보러 갈 거예요.
examples.en: I'm going to see an art exhibition this weekend.
The exhibition runs for a week starting today.
The school held an exhibition of students' works.
I found a painting I liked at the exhibition.
There is no admission fee for that exhibition.

examples.ko: 친구와 함께 전람회장에 갔더니 사람이 정말 많았어요.
examples.en: I went to the exhibition hall with a friend and it was really crowded.

explain: '전시회'와 비슷하지만 전람회는 조금 격식 있게 들리고, 일상 대화에서는 '전시회'를 더 자주 써요. 상품과 산업을 크게 보여 주는 행사는 '박람회'라고 해요. 발음은 [절람회]예요.
explain_en: It is similar to '전시회', but 전람회 sounds a bit more formal, and '전시회' is more common in everyday talk. A large event showing products and industries is called '박람회'. It is pronounced [절람회].

examples.en: The athlete aims at the target.
I aimed the water gun at my friend.

examples.ko: 먼저 조준하고 숨을 멈춘 뒤에 쏘세요.
examples.en: Aim first, hold your breath, and then shoot.
I aimed slowly and shot the arrow.
When aiming, I close one eye.
The gaze aiming at the target is sharp.

explain: '과녁을 조준하다'처럼 대상을 '을/를'로 받아요. 일상에서는 '겨냥하다'도 자주 쓰고, 비유로 '시장을 겨냥하다'라고 하면 '조준하다'보다 더 자연스러워요. 총, 활, 물총을 쏘기 직전의 동작이에요.
explain_en: It takes its target with the object particle, as in '과녁을 조준하다'. In daily speech '겨냥하다' is also common, and figuratively '시장을 겨냥하다' sounds more natural than 조준하다. It is the action right before shooting a gun, bow, or water gun.

examples.en: I sang songs with my friends in front of the campfire.
We had a campfire on the last day of the retreat.
The light of the campfire was really warm.
The campfire was canceled because of rain.
We sat around the campfire and roasted marshmallows.
The kids are looking forward to the campfire the most.

explain: 캠핑이나 수련회에서 모여 앉아 즐기는 불 행사를 말해요. 불 자체는 '모닥불'이라고 해요. '캠프파이어를 하다'처럼 행사 느낌으로 쓰고, '모닥불을 피우다'처럼 불을 지핀다는 느낌으로도 써요.
explain_en: It refers to the event of gathering around a fire at a camp or retreat. The fire itself is '모닥불'. You say '캠프파이어를 하다' for the event and '모닥불을 피우다' for lighting the fire.

examples.en: Beaches usually close at the end of August.
What time does the amusement park close?

examples.ko: 날씨가 추워져서 올해는 일찍 폐장하기로 했어요.
examples.en: Because it got cold, they decided to close early this year.

examples.ko: 시장이 벌써 폐장했으니까 내일 다시 가요.
examples.en: The market has already closed, so let's go again tomorrow.

examples.ko: 스키장은 봄이 되면 폐장하는 곳이 많아요.
examples.en: Many ski resorts close when spring comes.
Let's have one last swim before it closes for the season.

explain: 주로 해수욕장, 스키장, 시장, 놀이공원처럼 계절이나 하루의 영업을 끝낼 때 써요. 반대말은 '개장하다'예요. 가게 문을 닫을 때는 보통 '문을 닫다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: It is mainly used when places like beaches, ski resorts, markets and amusement parks end their season or their day. The opposite is '개장하다' (to open). For a normal shop, people usually say '문을 닫다'.

dis.h: a venue shuts for the season

p.n: The passive stresses that it is closed by schedule; the active one is just 'closes'. Both are fine.

examples.ko: 그 피아니스트는 다음 달에 오케스트라와의 협연을 앞두고 있어요.
examples.en: That pianist has a concerto performance with an orchestra coming up next month.

examples.ko: 이번 콘서트에서는 두 가수의 협연 무대가 있어요.
examples.en: This concert will have a joint stage with two singers.
We gathered from the morning to rehearse the joint performance.

examples.ko: 그 바이올리니스트는 협연 경험이 아주 많아요.
examples.en: That violinist has a lot of experience performing with orchestras.

examples.ko: 협연 덕분에 평소 듣기 어려운 조합을 즐겼어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the joint performance, I enjoyed a combination I rarely get to hear.
The joint performance by the student and teacher was really moving.

explain: 독주자가 오케스트라나 다른 연주자와 함께 무대에 서는 것을 말해요. 모두 비슷한 역할로 함께 연주하는 '합주'와는 조금 달라요.
explain_en: It refers to a soloist appearing on stage together with an orchestra or other performers. It is a little different from '합주', where everyone plays together in similar roles.
